title: The Ravine at Pathargarh
logline: Bhairav Singh's men take the grain train where the line bends through Teen Mod — and the one man who swears the ravine cannot be reached in time is the man who writes the timings.
artStyle: Ochre dust and bleached khaki, long shadows at four in the afternoon, heat haze over stone, a single red scarf against the ravine wall.

cast.name: Subedar Hari Pawar
cast.persona: Retired, one arm, and the only man in the district Bhairav has never bought. Asks the obvious question twice.

cast.name: Station Master Girdhari Lal
cast.persona: Helpful to a fault, quotes his own register as scripture, and has never been asked to prove a line of it.

acts.title: Bhairav's Alibi
acts.goal: Girdhari swears Bhairav was at the Pathargarh temple ten minutes before the train was hit, six kilometres up the line. Set the reckoning board to the speed that would take, and show him what he is claiming.

prediction.question: Girdhari says Bhairav walked the six kilometres from the temple to Teen Mod in ten minutes. Before you work anything out — is that possible?
options: Yes, uphill is slow but 6 km is a short distance
No, that implies a speed no one walks
Only if he ran the whole way

acts.explainAfter: Average speed is total distance over total time, and it does not care how the walk felt. Six kilometres in ten minutes is 36 km/h. A person tops out near 25 km/h on flat ground for seconds at a time, so it is the timing that is wrong, not the walker. That is why an average is evidence: it can be impossible.

spec.win: claimedSpeed >= impliedSpeed - 1 && claimedSpeed <= impliedSpeed + 1 && impliedSpeed > walkMaxKmh

band.label: Green is what a person can actually walk. Dalvi's timings land outside it — that is the lie.

dialogue.speaker: Station Master Girdhari Lal
dialogue.line: He was at the temple at ten past. The train was hit at twenty past. Six kilometres of ravine road between them.

dialogue.speaker: Subedar Hari Pawar
dialogue.line: And who wrote down ten past, Station Master?

dialogue.speaker: Station Master Girdhari Lal
dialogue.line: I did. As I have for nineteen years. The register does not lie.

dialogue.speaker: Subedar Hari Pawar
dialogue.line: Then set the board to what your own register implies, and we will see what nineteen years is worth.

signed-timetable.speaker: Station Master Girdhari Lal
lines: Bhairav Singh, seen at Pathargarh temple — ten past the hour.
Grain train stopped at Teen Mod — twenty past. Six kilometres of ravine road between them.
Signed, G. Lal, Station Master. Nineteen years of them, in this same hand.

beat.won: Girdhari sits down very suddenly. The register stays open on the desk.
beat.lost: Girdhari folds his arms. "Nineteen years, Subedar."
beat.speaker: Subedar Hari Pawar

steps: Walk to the reckoning board — WASD or the arrow keys.
Press E to take hold of the needle.
Left and right move it. It starts inside the green band, and the answer is not.
Press E again to put the reading to Girdhari.

acts.title: The Runaway Wagon
acts.goal: They cut a grain wagon loose on the falling grade above Pathargarh. You have a brake and nothing else. Ride it down and stop it inside the siding, short of the water tower.

prediction.question: You move the marker 10 m further down the grade. The stopping distance…
options: Shrinks — braking starts later so there is less left to lose
Stays the same — the brakes do not know where they are
Grows — the train has longer to pick up speed

acts.explainAfter: Once the brakes bite, the distance to stop depends on how fast you were going and how hard you can brake — not on where you started braking. Moving the marker moves the whole stop; it does not shorten it. That is v² = u² + 2as read backwards: double the speed and you quadruple the distance.

visual.xLabel: time since she was let go (s)

band.label: Braking later moves the whole stop down the hill. It never makes it shorter.

dialogue.speaker: Subedar Hari Pawar
dialogue.line: The siding ends at the water tower. Overrun it and the wagon goes into Teen Mod.

dialogue.speaker: Station Master Girdhari Lal
dialogue.line: Brake at the top. Everyone brakes at the top.

dialogue.speaker: Subedar Hari Pawar
dialogue.line: At the top she is still doing sixteen. Let us see what sixteen costs.

bindings.label: brake
bindings.prompt: let the brakes off and ride her down

beat.won: She comes to rest with the tower still dry. Girdhari says nothing at all.
beat.lost: Water everywhere and the siding points bent. Pawar does not look at you.
beat.speaker: Subedar Hari Pawar

steps: Press F to let the brakes off and ride her down.
Hold SPACE to brake. When you let go is the whole act.
F runs it again and keeps your old attempts beside the line; R clears them.

acts.title: Across Teen Mod
acts.goal: Bhairav's rider is on the far ledge and already walking. Get the grain-office strongbox across the ravine to Pawar’s men before he reaches it.

prediction.question: You double the forward speed and keep the upward speed the same. The satchel…
options: Stays in the air twice as long
Lands twice as far, in the same flight time
Lands twice as far and twice as late

acts.explainAfter: Horizontal and vertical motion do not talk to each other. Gravity only ever works on the vertical, so the time in the air is set by the upward speed and the drop — and the forward speed just decides how much ground that time buys you. Height buys seconds; speed spends them.

spec.win: landX >= ledgeNear && landX <= ledgeFar && flight <= banditEta

band.label: Upward speed sets how long it flies. He is walking the whole time it is up there.

dialogue.speaker: Subedar Hari Pawar
dialogue.line: My men are on the far ledge. The rider gets there in under three seconds.

dialogue.speaker: Subedar Hari Pawar
dialogue.line: Height buys hang time, Station Master. It does not buy distance.

beat.won: The box hits the ledge a clear stride ahead of him. He turns and runs.
beat.lost: He picks it up without breaking stride and is gone into the rocks.
beat.speaker: Subedar Hari Pawar

steps: Drag away from it and let go. Further is harder, higher is steeper.
R to take the shot again.

twist: There were no dacoits on the ravine road that night until Girdhari needed some. He writes the timings, he signs them, and he reads them back to you — nineteen years of a hand nobody has ever once checked. Bhairav only ever had to be where the register said he was.
